clue.text: Continuous pain? One must ring hospital

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the word for one goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A patient in constant pain insists that somebody phone the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull persistent hurt is exactly what this word names; the question mark nods at the loose fit.

clue.text: Bargain for a nice tip at races

indicators.note: the letters race about, rushing into a new order

explanation.surface: A punter hopes for a good tip at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races' is a horse-racing meeting on the surface but signals the letters of A NICE TIP AT scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain for something is to expect or foresee it, as in 'more than I bargained for'.

clue.text: Within reach of Hooghly's banks?

parts.note: the outside letters of Hooghly, its banks, joined by the word for plus, give a word for within reach

explanation.surface: Is it close to the banks of the Hooghly river in India?
explanation.walkthrough: The Hooghly is a river in West Bengal; its banks are its first and last letters, linked with a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by and convenient to use is within reach.

clue.text: PA a fellow uses in resort

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A personal assistant and her colleague spend time at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday spot but is re-sort, the signal to rearrange; PA is a personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary who takes dictation, an old-fashioned personal assistant.

clue.text: Chap overcoming doubt points to platform

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: a chap is a man
an if is a doubt, as in no ifs
E and S are compass points, east and south
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man conquers his misgivings and points towards the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'platform' is a political programme, not a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published programme of policies is its platform.

clue.text: Somewhat unorthodox British leader

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the next word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A British leader is described as a bit of a maverick.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick North was Prime Minister of Great Britain from 1770 to 1782.

clue.text: Former winner, it's believed, maintains pressure —— and that's not all

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the certainty holds the pressure letter

parts.note: a cert is a racing certainty, a horse believed sure to win
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A former champion, thought a sure thing, keeps up the pressure, and there is more to come.
explanation.walkthrough: CERT is short for certainty, a horse thought bound to win.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is only part of the whole text, so not all of it.

clue.text: Ordered this local fabric

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, newly arranged

explanation.surface: Someone orders a locally made fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas or other strong cloth used to make a ship's sails is a fabric.

clue.text: Forward, first to score goal

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football forward is the first to score a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' suggests a striker but is the verb to send on, as with mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter or message is to dispatch it onward.

clue.text: Put off by old women's name for a residential area?

indicators.note: off means out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone is deterred by the name an old woman gave a housing area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges PUT into UPT, followed by O, W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: In American use the residential districts away from the business centre are called this.

clue.text: After short time at home, a single person takes hold of drill — right tool?

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
in means at home

indicators.note: the word for one person grips the drill letters inside itself

parts.note: one single person is ONE
PE, physical education, is drill in a school gym

explanation.surface: Someone who lives alone gets home and picks up a drill, wondering if it is the right tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' suggests a power tool but is PE, school exercises; 'takes hold of' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for opening cans is a kitchen tool, hence the question mark for a modest example.

clue.text: Landmark seen in Australian port when docked

indicators.note: docking cuts off the tail, so the port's final letter is dropped

parts.note: Cairns is a port in Queensland, Australia

explanation.surface: A ship coming into an Australian harbour spots a familiar landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship at a quay, but it means cut short: CAIRNS loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of stones piled up as a marker on a hill or path is a landmark.

clue.text: Keen to run back and cause unnecessary alarm

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief

indicators.note: running back means the word for flow is read backwards

parts.note: to run, as liquid does, is to flow

explanation.surface: An anxious person, eager to retreat, ends up setting off a false alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like 'eager' but is the verb to wail; 'back' turns FLOW into WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: From the fable of the shepherd boy, the idiom means raising false alarms repeatedly.

clue.text: Introduction to Homer, or magnificent Roman poet

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
ace is slang for excellent or magnificent

explanation.surface: A reader is offered a choice between starting with Homer or a great Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintus Horatius Flaccus, author of the Odes, was a celebrated Latin poet of Augustus's time.

clue.text: After year in unimaginative surroundings, escape regardless of circumstances

indicators.note: the year letter is placed in the word for unimaginative

parts.note: inane means silly or empty-headed, lacking ideas
a vent is an outlet or escape, as for steam

explanation.surface: After a year in dull surroundings, someone escapes no matter what.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' only adds to the picture of the dull place; 'in' alone signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whatever happens, whatever the situation turns out to be.

clue.text: Act firmly to gain momentum

definitions.meaning: to insist and refuse to give way
to press the accelerator hard and speed up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to assert authority, and literally a driver pressing the pedal to accelerate.

clue.text: Omitting being upset about wife carrying on

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the wife letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A husband is upset at leaving out his wife, who is having an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' rearranges OMITTING to TOTIMING, which goes about W.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying on means having an affair, and being unfaithful to a partner is this.

clue.text: Exhibiting unacceptable behaviour, female supporting leader of opposition in sketch

indicators.note: the pair of letters is placed inside the sketch

parts.note: an outline is a rough sketch

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman backing the opposition leader in a satirical sketch behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: F supports O (from 'leader of opposition') in a down light, giving OF inside OUTLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving improperly, beyond what is acceptable, is described by this idiom.

clue.text: Being excessively hot in kitchen, somehow faced the situation stoically

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: the letters are arranged somehow, any old way, so they are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cook, sweltering in the heat of the kitchen, bore it without complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' signals the rearrangement; 'took it on the chin' comes from boxing, absorbing a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxing idiom means to absorb a blow, so to accept a setback bravely and without complaint.

clue.text: Look at source of problem in cricket, say

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the creature

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone examines what is causing trouble in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' is the sport on the surface but the chirping insect in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to look at carefully.

clue.text: Call in centre of St Helier for nail polish

indicators.note: the word for call goes inside the central letters
the centre is the middle pair of letters of the whole name

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A request is made in central St Helier for nail varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helier is the capital of Jersey; 'centre of' takes the middle of the name read as one run of eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy coating for fingernails is called nail enamel, so the word serves for the polish.

clue.text: Concern after conclusion of government paper

indicators.note: the word for concern comes after the letter from government
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: an issue is a matter of concern

explanation.surface: Worries persist after a government's term ends, as recorded in an official paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft thin paper, as used for wrapping or as a handkerchief, goes by this name.

clue.text: Keen listener describing good ending to programme

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the ear goes round the letters

parts.note: an ear is a listener

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic listener gives a good account of how a show ended.
explanation.walkthrough: G and E (end of 'programme') go inside EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen are synonyms meaning enthusiastic.

clue.text: Flimsy, low quality paper in folder

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
a rag is a disparaging name for a poor newspaper

explanation.surface: A cheap, flimsy sheet of paper has been tucked into a folder.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a disparaging name for a tabloid newspaper, hence low quality paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily broken or delicate is fragile, close in sense to flimsy.

clue.text: Model and I do business

parts.note: taken as written
to deal is to trade or do business

explanation.surface: A fashion model and I work together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example, a model to imitate.

clue.text: Stole from head of Winchester — charge follows

indicators.note: the word for charge comes after the letter from Winchester
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: Something was stolen from the headmaster of Winchester, and a charge comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb but is the noun, a shawl; Winchester is a famous English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a scarf or shawl, and a wrap is the same sort of garment.

clue.text: Put up beams in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Workers install lighting beams in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' suggests construction timbers, but they are rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up or erect it is to raise it.

clue.text: One included in piece by first lady about legendary wife

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for a firearm

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun
I is the Roman numeral one
Eve was the first woman in Genesis
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A First Lady features in an article about a wife from legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like an article but is slang for a gun; 'first lady' is not a president's wife but EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's queen in Arthurian legend, whose affair with Lancelot is famous.

clue.text: Compelling work produced by foremost of painters, mature artist

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to age is to mature
J.M.W. Turner was a great English painter

explanation.surface: A gripping masterpiece by a leading painter, a mature artist in his prime.
explanation.definitionFit: A book so gripping that one keeps turning the leaves is called this.

clue.text: Dummy left in baby's bed

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a baby's bed with sides

explanation.surface: A baby's dummy has been left lying in the cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dummy' suggests a baby's pacifier, matching the cot, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person, as is dummy.
